graft.title: baseline render still writes hooks into a repo's .claude/settings.local.json; the 2026.10.3 conduct says repos carry none
graft.need: vg-paradigms release 2026.10.3's conduct (Care) now says: Tend's hooks are per machine, installed once in the user's own Claude settings (`tend env context --install-hook`); a repo carries none and they're never added to a repo's settings file. In vg-dotfiles (vghydra, 2026-10-23), `tend baseline render --write` after `tend baseline upgrade` to 2026.10.3 still wrote 13 hooks into the repo's `.claude/settings.local.json` (tend-activity, tend-guard-*, tend-context, tend-session-end, tend-idle, tend-busy). The user-level settings (~/.claude-personal/settings.json) have none yet, so nothing runs twice today; once the user installs them user-level as the conduct says, every session here would run both. Needed: render stops writing per-repo hooks (or removes the ones it wrote) when the baseline's conduct puts them user-level, and says to run `tend env context --install-hook` if the user-level ones are missing.
graft.use_case: Every repo on Tend re-renders after a baseline upgrade; following the new conduct today means the user hand-deletes the hooks render just wrote (agents may not edit hook settings), in every repo, after every render.

answer.text: Done in tend fdf25ba: `tend baseline render` declares no Claude Code hooks for a repo any more, so the ones it wrote into .claude/settings.local.json are taken out (as leftovers, where they're as Tend wrote them) on the next `render --write`, and render says to run `tend env context --install-hook` when your user-level settings don't run Tend's hooks yet. The user-level install now covers everything a repo's rendering did: the context, file writes, idle and busy, session end, and a guard hook at every event (a repo's own guards may use any). Order for each machine: the user runs `tend env context --install-hook` once, then each repo's `render --write` drops its copies; nothing runs twice in between, since render stops declaring them only where it writes.

updates.text: A correction to the answer: between `tend env context --install-hook` and a repo's next `render --write`, that repo's sessions run the hooks twice (the user-level ones and the repo's copies), so render each repo right after installing. The reverse order leaves the repo with no hooks until the install, so install first.
